name: invoke-sqlcmd
description: SQL Server / Azure SQL — run PowerShell Invoke-Sqlcmd commands, signed in with a stored Entra ID (Azure AD) credential or SQL login. Only commands beginning with Invoke-Sqlcmd are accepted.

settings.label: Sign-in mode
settings.description: Which stored credential this plugin signs in with. Only the fields the chosen mode uses are shown below.

options.label: Entra service principal (client secret)
options.description: An app registration's client ID + secret. Needs the tenant ID, client ID and client secret. The principal must exist as a user in the database (CREATE USER [app-name] FROM EXTERNAL PROVIDER).

options.label: Entra user (username + password)
options.description: An Entra ID account without MFA, e.g. a dedicated service account. Needs the tenant ID, username and password. Accounts with MFA or conditional access cannot sign in this way.

options.label: Managed identity (this machine)
options.description: The Azure VM / App Service identity the server runs under. No secret is stored. For a user-assigned identity, put its client ID in 'Client ID'.

options.label: SQL login (username + password)
options.description: Classic SQL Server authentication, not Entra ID. Needs the username and password.

settings.label: Apply the credential
settings.description: Whether the stored credential is applied to every Invoke-Sqlcmd automatically, or only when a command references it ($SqlAccessToken / $SqlCredential).

options.label: Automatically
options.description: Every Invoke-Sqlcmd is signed in with the stored credential unless the command passes its own (-AccessToken, -Credential, -Username/-Password or -ConnectionString).

options.label: Only when the command references it
options.description: Nothing is injected. A command uses the stored credential by writing -AccessToken $SqlAccessToken or -Credential $SqlCredential, exactly as an ordinary script would.

settings.label: Entra tenant ID
settings.description: Directory (tenant) GUID or verified domain (contoso.onmicrosoft.com). 'common' does not work for a service principal.

settings.label: Client ID
settings.description: Service principal mode: the app registration's Application (client) ID. Managed identity mode: a user-assigned identity's client ID (leave empty for system-assigned). Entra user mode: optional public client app to sign in through; empty uses the Azure CLI's well-known public client.

settings.label: Username
settings.description: Entra user mode: the UPN (svc-sql@contoso.com). SQL login mode: the login name. The password goes in the credential field below.

settings.label: Default server
settings.description: Used as -ServerInstance when a command does not name one, e.g. myserver.database.windows.net. Also what Authenticate connects to in order to prove the credential works. Optional.

settings.label: Default database
settings.description: Used as -Database when a command does not name one. Optional; without it the login's default database (master on Azure SQL) is used.

secrets.label: Service principal client secret
secrets.description: The secret's *Value* (shown once in Azure), not its Secret ID. Write-only; encrypted at rest. Client secrets expire — check that first if sign-in suddenly fails.

secrets.label: Password
secrets.description: The password for 'Username'. Write-only; encrypted at rest.
